requirements.text: Analyze the hybrid retrieval mechanisms available in PostgreSQL pgvector for enterprise RAG, including how vector similarity search can be combined with lexical search and how fusion methods such as reciprocal rank fusion and weighted fusion are supported or implemented.

Analyze index selection and tradeoffs in PostgreSQL pgvector for enterprise RAG, comparing index types such as HNSW and IVFFlat on recall, latency, memory usage, build time, filtered search behavior, update costs, and suitability for different workload scales.

Analyze engineering limitations of PostgreSQL pgvector in enterprise RAG workloads, including scalability, concurrency, multi-tenancy, access control filtering, index maintenance, operational complexity, cost, and reliability constraints.

evidences.title: The Postgres Developer's Guide to Vector Index Tradeoffs | Tiger Data
evidences.content: Compared with HNSW, IVFFlat is usually lighter to build and maintain. Inserts are simpler because adding a vector means assigning it to a list rather than updating a graph of neighboring nodes.

claims.text: In pgvector, IVFFlat is described as usually lighter to build and maintain than HNSW, with simpler inserts because adding a vector means assigning it to a list rather than updating a graph of neighboring nodes.

IVFFlat recall is described as more sensitive to tuning; increasing probes gives the query more chances to find true nearest neighbors but pushes it closer to a broader scan, so tuning involves finding the lowest probes value that still meets a recall target.
